learning_outcomes.text: Know the structure and architecture of digital computers.
Understand the meaning of information technology terms (information representation, number systems, algorithms).
Understand and be able to apply fundamental concepts of procedural programming and modeling.
Master important language constructs of the ANSI C/C++ programming language, especially common control structures and data structures.
Be able to handle all standard data types as well as initial custom data types, understand algorithmic thought patterns, and implement them in concrete programs.

syllabus_topics: Computer systems and informatics, machine models (Von-Neumann, Virtual Machines and Operating Systems)
Number systems (Decimal/Binary/Octal/Hexadecimal system) and character codes (ASCII, ANSI, EBCDI, Unicode)
Introduction to the ANSI-C/C++ programming language
Program structure, constants, basic data types
Practical laboratory exercises deepening the content of MECB141 Lecture Computer Science 1

assessment_methods.method: Examination prerequisite XP (report, elaboration of a programming example or similar)

assessment_rules: Student knowledge is assessed via a graded written module examination of 90 minutes. The module grade for MECB140 corresponds to the grade for MECB141. MECB142 Labor Informatik 1 is assessed semester-long through ungraded laboratory work and certified. An examination prerequisite (XP) will be defined at the beginning of the semester.
